methodology: Individual verse first-pass screening. Prior draft PR #319 ends 9:25. Candidate references are unverified research leads only; no direct-dependence inference or public promotion. This staging file is not an authoritative merged coverage ledger.

records.theme: Divine reassurance and unseen hosts after Hunayn

candidates.difference: Elisha's servant sees a mountain filled with fiery horses and chariots; Qur'an 9:26 speaks of tranquility and unseen hosts in a specific seventh-century battle. Neither text names the other's event.

records.question: Compare 9:26 with 8:9–12 internally; inspect Hebrew and Syriac versions before deciding whether an external motif is sufficiently specific.
General repentance language alone does not warrant attaching a source. Reassess only if a distinctive antecedent is identified.

records.theme: Exclusion of polytheists from the Sacred Mosque after this year

candidates.difference: Numbers restricts sanctuary approach and priestly duties within Israelite cultic hierarchy; Qur'an 9:28 addresses polytheists' access to al-Masjid al-Haram and anticipated economic hardship. Neither is the same legal category.
Isaiah envisages foreigners joining covenant worship at God's house; Qur'an 9:28 restricts a specified religious group from the sanctuary. Historical institutions and groups differ.

records.question: Research documented pre-Islamic Arabian sanctuary access separately; verify Hebrew textual context, relevant dating and critical translations.

records.theme: Fighting People of the Book and jizya

candidates.difference: Deuteronomy prescribes offering peace and imposing forced labor on certain conquered cities; Qur'an 9:29 addresses fighting specified People of the Book until jizya is paid. Different groups, conditions and institutional terminology.

records.question: Check Arabic jizya and an yad, early interpretive variation, late antique tax institutions and legal historical context; avoid treating Deuteronomy as direct source.

records.theme: Claims concerning Ezra and Messiah as son of God

candidates.difference: John contains a confession concerning Jesus as Son of God in some textual traditions; Qur'an 9:30 attributes this claim to Christians while also reporting a distinct claim about Ezra among Jews. No verified Jewish source for an Ezra-son-of-God doctrine is established here.

records.question: Inspect Greek variants of John 1:34 and relevant christological formulations; investigate the Ezra assertion without inventing a Jewish antecedent, and separate late antique polemic from primary witness evidence.
